subject: Evidence sync: renewal timeline, SOC 2 coverage confirmation & CAIQ/SIG asks
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@acmehealth.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwoodai.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 / CAIQ & renewal evidence timing

Hi Jasmine,

We're kicking off the renewal procurement for Acme Health and our InfoSec team needs the following before our internal approval meeting on 2027-06-02: 

- Latest SOC 2 Type II report (period covered + audit firm)
- If the report doesn't cover the renewal window, a bridge letter / attestation that covers through 2027-09-30
- Completed CAIQ extract (we'll validate select controls) and SIG-lite responses for privacy/security controls
- A short list of evidence items we may request (access logs, change control summary, retention policy PDF)

Can you confirm whether you can provide the SOC 2 Type II report, and whether Redwood can issue a bridge attestation? Also please confirm estimated delivery dates for the full CAIQ extract and any attachments.

Thanks — tight timeline on our side.

Best,
Lina 
Lina Park
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com

Hi Lina — thanks for the heads up and the checklist. Looping in Rishi (security/compliance) and Vivek (customer success) so we can align on scope and timing.

Quick answers up front:
- We have a SOC 2 Type II report from the 2026 audit covering 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, audited by Brightline LLP. We can share the PDF by EOD Thursday (2027-05-20).
- We can provide a bridge attestation that confirms continuous controls since the last report and extends coverage through 2027-09-30. Draft can be shared for review by Friday (2027-05-21).
- CAIQ extract: we maintain a prefilled CAIQ spreadsheet that we can export for you. Expect the first pass by Friday; we can refine to the specific control IDs you raise.

Two clarifying q's to help prioritize evidence:
1) For the bridge, do you need auditor-signed language or is a Redwood-signed attestation sufficient for Acme's procurement?
2) Which specific CAIQ sections are must-haves for your InfoSec review (e.g., encryption, logging, key management, data residency)? A short list will let us expedite.

Plan: Rishi will prepare the SOC PDF + a draft bridge attestation. Vivek will coordinate the CAIQ extract and the minimal evidence pack. I'll own delivery and follow the DocuSign flow if needed.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodai.com

From: Lina Park <lina.park@acmehealth.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwoodai.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / CAIQ & renewal evidence timing

Thanks Jasmine — that timeline would work for Acme. Answers to your questions:

1) Our InfoSec team would prefer auditor-signed bridge language when available, but in prior renewals we've accepted vendor-signed attestations for interim coverage as long as it's explicit about the period and control continuity. We'll flag if an auditor signature becomes a blocker.
2) Must-have CAIQ sections for this renewal: 
   - SI (Security Incident Management)
   - SC (System and Communications Protection / Encryption at rest & transit)
   - IA (Identity & Access Management)
   - CM (Change Management)

If you can provide the SOC PDF + a vendor-signed bridge attestation by 2027-05-21 and the CAIQ extract by 2027-05-21 (first pass), our reviewers will begin validation on 2027-05-24 and we should be in position to confirm procurement terms by 2027-06-02.

Also, we will likely request at least one sample evidence item (e.g., a redacted change control log) during validation — predictable spot check, not a full audit — please flag any PII concerns.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Lina

Subject: Re: SOC 2 / CAIQ & renewal evidence timing

Hi Lina — Rishi here from Redwood Security. Thanks for the priorities — responding with the specifics and attachments.

What I'm attaching in this thread: 
- redwood_soc2_type2_2026.pdf — SOC 2 Type II report (2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31; Brightline LLP)
- soc2_bridge_attestation_draft.docx — vendor-signed bridge attestation (draft) extending control coverage to 2027-09-30. We can add auditor language if you tell us that will be required.
- redwood_caiaq_extract.xlsx — CAIQ extract with columns filtered for SI, SC, IA, CM as requested.

Delivery notes and evidence plan: 
- SOC PDF: final attached (redacted where appropriate).
- Bridge attestation: draft attached. We propose Redwood-signed attestation for procurement. If Acme insists on auditor-signed bridge, we will need to engage Brightline — that typically adds 7-10 business days and incurs an out-of-cycle fee. Please advise.
- CAIQ extract: first-pass completed for requested sections. We highlighted (yellow) controls where evidence is commonly requested and added pointers to where evidence lives (internal IDs).
- Sample evidence: We can provide a redacted change control summary and a short access-logs extract (last 30 days) under an NDA. Let us know which you prefer first.

Next steps we propose: 
1) Lina confirms whether vendor-signed bridge is acceptable.
2) If yes, we finalise attestation and send for signature (anticipated turnaround 24-48 hours).
3) We upload CAIQ + sample evidence to your shared drive link and open a secure share for logs if needed.

If you need an on-call walk-through with our security team, we can schedule 30 minutes Monday 2027-05-24.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodai.com
